head: fb79950
target: Let multeval drive aigent as a command and grade the run from the files it leaves: the hard-coded live test becomes scenario data, every run is recorded as a result directory, and the verdict on engine bugs and model bets comes from those files alone.
incidental: package.json and package-lock.json: the aigent command entry and the npm script that loads .env
test/boundary.test.ts: the import guard learns the new eval file names
test/scenarios/: the first scenario file and the fixture plugins it loads
the faux-model plumbing the new tests share

questions.prompt: aigent run writes the result directory, then grades the files it just wrote, not the run in memory. What does the round trip prove?

options.label: The files can drift from memory, and the check must catch the difference.
The check runs in a fresh process, so it cannot see the run in memory.
The directory alone is enough to grade the run, for a grader that was not there.
Reading the files back is cheaper than keeping the whole run in memory.

key_points: The files alone are enough to grade the run.
Every run proves it, because the command grades the files it just wrote.
multeval reads only the files, and it never watched the run.

questions.prompt: The old live test logged most of what it saw, so an engine bug and a model mistake looked alike. How does the report split them now?

options.label: Invariants check the engine code, and behaviors check the model code.
Invariants must hold in every run; behaviors are rates over trials, and cost is never judged.
An invariant failure stops the run at once; a behavior failure is only logged.
Invariants hold in native mode, and behaviors are the bets of dispatch mode.

key_points: Invariants are engine properties every run must keep; one failure is an engine bug.
Behaviors are the design's bets on the model, measured as rates over trials.
Cost is reported and never judged.
The exit code carries the split: an engine bug fails it, and behaviors never do.

questions.prompt: A run stops at its first prompt, which ended in a provider error. The scenario expects the model to use a tool on that prompt and on a later one. Which expectations end in a skip?

options.label: The invariants, because the run stopped early.
The use expectation on the failed prompt, because the prompt never finished.
The cost of the first prompt, because no answer came back.
The use expectation on the later prompt, because the run never reached it.

key_points: A behavior skips when its step never ran or its prompt ended early.
A behavior skips when its precondition never happened, such as an enable that never came.
A skip is left out of the behavior's rate, so the rate counts only trials that had the chance.
Invariants never skip.

questions.prompt: The engine hands the runner a raw secret, not the redacted form. What do the written files hold, and what can a grader learn?

options.label: The raw secret, so only a key holder can audit the files.
A leak mark naming the secret; the grader sees the leak without the key.
Nothing; the runner drops any string that carried the secret.
The session's redacted mark, so the leak looks like a normal redaction.

key_points: No file holds the raw secret; the scrub leaves a mark that names it.
The leak mark differs from a normal redaction, so a leak never hides as one.
The secret-free invariant fails on the mark, so a leak is an engine bug.
A grader can find and name the leak without ever holding the key.

questions.prompt: The runner joins neighboring text deltas into one string before the scrub runs. Why does the scrub need whole strings?

options.label: The events file cannot hold two text events for one turn.
The run log should read as whole messages rather than as stream fragments.
A secret can arrive split across two deltas, and neither delta alone holds it.
The scrub runs faster on one long string than on many short ones.

key_points: The scrub replaces whole strings, so it must see a secret as one string.
A secret can be split across stream deltas; scrubbing each delta alone would miss it.
The joined text event is what the log and the files keep.

questions.prompt: The checks read the transcript and the session events together. Which of these can a check see only in the transcript?

options.label: The tool calls that ran, with their results.
The plugins enabled when a session was created.
The enable records the model caused during a prompt.
A tool call the engine rejected before it ran.

key_points: Records written when a session is created reach no listener; only the transcript holds them.
A call rejected before it runs leaves no tool event, only an error result in the transcript.
A check that read only the events would misjudge what was enabled and what was rejected.

questions.prompt: The runner dies while it writes the result directory. What is on disk, and what can a reader mistake for a run?
key_points: The result directory is all or nothing: it exists only once whole.
A crash leaves only a sibling with a partial suffix, which no reader mistakes for a run.
The rename into place is the last step, so the directory never appears half-written.

questions.prompt: A scenario names a tool its plugin set lacks, and a secret that is unset. When does the run refuse it, and why then?

options.label: After the first prompt fails, so the refusal carries the model's own error.
At the end, in the report, so the run still measures the failure.
Before the first session opens, so a typo costs no model call.
Never; the runner starts the session and skips the steps it cannot run.

key_points: Secrets, plugin sets and the names they rely on are checked before the first session opens.
A doomed or mistyped scenario costs no model call.
Every problem is reported at once, each at its place in the file, so one round of fixes.
The command also refuses an existing result directory before it reads the scenario.

questions.prompt: A new engine property arrives that every run must keep, whatever the model does. Where does it go, and what must come with it?
key_points: It goes into the invariants table; the report's invariant list comes from that table.
Both case tables are typed by the check names, so the build fails until the new check has a passing and a failing case.
Its failing case must assert the evidence that names the mistake.

questions.prompt: A run's last prompt times out, and an invariant failed on an earlier step. Which of these hold when the command finishes?

options.label: The result directory is written, holding the steps that ran, and it is checked.
The timed-out prompt's behaviors count as failures, because the model let the timeout happen.
The command exits 1, because the invariant failure wins over the early stop.
The report says the run is not complete.

key_points: An invariant failure exits 1, which wins over the exit 3 of an early stop.
A run that stops early is still written and still checked, over the steps that ran.
The report says the run is not complete, so a caller can tell a stop from a bug.
The behaviors on the stopped prompt skip; a stop is not a model failure.
